newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian stocks little changed, Norilsk firms.
newsitem.headline: Russian stocks little changed, Norilsk firms.

text.p: Russian metals producer RAO Norilsky Nikel firmed while other stocks drifted in mostly directionless mid-afternoon trade on Wednesday, traders said, predicting little movement by the end of the session.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 516.34, slightly off Tuesday's record high close of 517.54.

"The market is becoming more and more dangerous for investors," said Prospekt's trading chief Andrei Ippolitov, adding that regional brokers were "sitting on shares" which in the past has signalled an imminent downward turn in the market.

Shares in Norilsk Nickel, which fell 17 percent on Tuesday after the company announced it would ask shareholders to approve doubling charter capital, were steady at $15.50 at 1030 GMT but off an earlier peak of $15.95. They closed at $15.00 on Tuesday.

Traders were unsure of the reason for the uptick, but ICFI's Dmitry Konov pointed to previous cases when Norilsk share price has bounced back from major drops as evidence of the stock's continuing attractiveness and growth potential.
Konov said a major market operator was supporting the price.

International long-distance carrier Rostelekom nudged up to $4.96 from $4.95 previously, national power company UES dipped to $0.4220 from $0.4236 and oil company LUKoil ticked up to $22.41 from $22.40.

Some traders said the market could rise by the end of the day, seeing Norilsk's recovery as a sign of broader market support. But others said Western investors, who sold heavily on Tuesday, would have the final say later in the day.

"We're not seeing aggressive selling yet, and there is even some interest in individual stocks, but it is a bit tentative," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze. "The market is fairly even so far and I think everything will depend on how New York opens."
